summary: 'What is F-Line Appeal?' (service code 0185) was answered as 'What is F-Line?' (service code 0178) -- a different, real code silently swapped for another one, in every tested attachment state.
preconditions: Reproduced BOTH with no attachment and with sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached, officer marun_chn@sis.tn.gov.in (SIS-002).
reproduction: No attachment: 'What is F-Line?' -> correctly 0178. 'What is F-Line Appeal?' -> still 0178, verbatim identical text, never mentions 0185.

With sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached (the screenshot's own scenario): 'What is F-Line Appeal?' asked as the FIRST message after upload -> 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.' (a DIFFERENT, compounding failure -- see ATTACH-INTERCEPT-001).
expected: Service code 0185 'F-Line Appeal', regardless of attachment state.
actual: 0178 (no attachment) or a flat attachment refusal (with attachment) -- 0185 was never once reached.
root_cause: backend/utils/helpers.py `find_service_code_by_name()` ran `_svc_name_alias_match()` (a bare substring check for 'f-line'/'f line'/'fline', returning 0178) BEFORE the real keyword-overlap scoring loop. That scoring loop, if ever reached, already resolves 'F-Line Appeal' correctly and uniquely to 0185 (its official name's two distinctive words, 'line' and 'appeal', both present, ratio 1.0, no other code qualifies) -- the alias short-circuit just never let it run.
verified_outcome: Live UI (fresh conversation, sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached), 2026-10-13 ~16:33: 'What is F-Line Appeal?' -> 'Service code 0185 = F-Line Appeal (F_LINE_APPEAL) -- TAMILNILAM urban service, field visit required. Files under it are held in your register.' Re-asked a second time later in the same conversation (04:18 PM) with the same correct result. Fix: `find_service_code_by_name()` now runs the keyword-scoring loop FIRST and falls back to `_svc_name_alias_match()` only when scoring finds nothing at all -- the exact case the alias exists for ('what is f-line?' alone, which scoring cannot resolve on its own). Regression test: SIS_ServiceCode_FileDB_Regression_Tests/test_servicecode_alias_collision.py (3/3 passing).

summary: The FIRST question asked right after ANY file upload -- even one with no connection to the file's content -- was answered from the attachment (and refused, since the file never mentioned the term) instead of reaching its own correct deterministic handler. This is the deeper, previously-undiagnosed cause of the screenshot's Turn 1 and Turn 2 failures.
preconditions: sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached (a plain service-code CSV, no mention of 'F-Line Appeal' anywhere in its text); fresh conversation, so the upload itself is the only prior turn.
reproduction: 2. Send: 'What is F-Line Appeal?' (first message after upload) -> 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.'
3. Send: 'What is the difference between F-Line and F-Line Appeal?' (second message) -> also 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.'
Exact reproduction of the task's own reported screenshot sequence, confirmed live before any code change.
expected: A bare service-code definition question, naming no file/document/attachment word, should reach `_service_code_lookup_answer()` exactly as it does with no file attached.
actual: Both questions were claimed by `attachment_qa.plan_answer()` and refused for lack of evidence in the file, even though `targets_attachment()` itself correctly returns False for both (verified directly: no doc-word, no filename, intent='service_code_lookup' not 'general_query').
root_cause: `backend/services/chatbot.py`'s upload endpoint (`backend/routers/chat.py`) saves the upload-confirmation message with `structured_context={"entity": "attachment", ...}`. `attachment_qa.attachment_topic_active()` reads the LAST assistant message's structured_data and returns True whenever its entity is 'attachment' -- which the upload confirmation always is, even though it is not a real file-answer turn. `plan_answer()`'s fallback block (for when `targets_attachment()` returns False) only bails out early for an application-number reference or a register-shaped question; everything else, including a bare service-code definition question, fell into `topic_active = True` and was wrongly answered from the file purely because the PRECEDING message happened to be an upload, not because the question was actually about it.
verified_outcome: Live UI, fresh conversation, sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached, 2026-10-13 ~16:33: Turn 1 ('What is F-Line Appeal?') -> correct 0185 answer. Turn 2 ('What is the difference...') -> correct dual-code answer. Fix: `plan_answer()`'s early-return condition in backend/services/attachment_qa.py now also exempts `intent == "service_code_lookup"`, the same way it already exempted an application-number reference and a register-shaped question -- a service-code definition has its own complete, file-independent deterministic answer and must never be routed through attachment evidence retrieval. Scope note: only `service_code_lookup` was exempted (the confirmed case); other deterministic intents were not tested under the same first-question-after-upload condition and may share this exposure -- flagged as a follow-up, not fixed here, per the minimal-change restriction.

summary: 'List all the service codes in this file.' (the screenshot's Turn 3) was refused with 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.' even though the CSV plainly has a service_code column with 5 values -- the identical question phrased as 'list the service_code column' answered correctly.
preconditions: sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached (header: row, service_code, service_description, application_number, status; 5 data rows: 0154, 0178, 0158, 0153, 0154).
reproduction: 1. Upload sis_svccode_fileA.csv (extraction_status='ok', 754 chars, 5 csv_rows, 1 chunk -- confirmed via the upload API response, so the failure is not an extraction/indexing problem).
2. Send: 'List all the service codes in this file.' -> 'I could not find this in the uploaded document.'
3. (diagnostic) Send: 'list the service_code column' -> correctly returns all 5 rows' values.
expected: A deterministic enumeration of the service_code column's 5 values, with source citation, from `csv_ops`'s 'computed, never narrated' engine.
actual: Refused outright by the ungrounded evidence-floor path; the deterministic CSV engine was never reached.
root_cause: `csv_ops.resolve_column()` required the normalised header text ('service code', from 'service_code') to be followed by a non-alphanumeric boundary; the natural plural 'service codes' in the question has a trailing 's' that is itself alphanumeric, so that boundary never closed and the full-header match failed. The fallback single-distinctive-word match then found the word 'service' in TWO columns (`service_code` AND `service_description`), so `resolve_column()` correctly refused to pick either rather than guess -- and `parse_csv_question()` therefore returned None, sending the question past the deterministic engine entirely.
verified_outcome: Live UI, fresh conversation, sis_svccode_fileA.csv attached, 2026-10-13 ~16:33: 'List all the service codes in this file.' -> deterministic table: 'row 1: 0154 / row 2: 0178 / row 3: 0158 / row 4: 0153 / row 5: 0154 [sis_svccode_fileA.csv, rows 1-5]' -- exact match to independently-established ground truth. Fix: `resolve_column()` in backend/services/csv_ops.py now allows an optional trailing 's' after the escaped header text before the boundary check, so 'service codes' matches the 'service_code' header directly and wins the full-header match before the ambiguous single-word fallback is ever reached. Regression test: SIS_ServiceCode_FileDB_Regression_Tests/test_csv_plural_column_resolution.py (3/3 passing).

summary: 'Compare the service codes in both files.' across two attached CSVs, previously answered with wrong per-file figures from the ungrounded LLM path (dropped a value, over-counted another, same root cause as CSVCOL-FLINE-001) -- now confirmed fixed as a direct side effect of the resolve_column() fix.
preconditions: sis_svccode_fileA.csv AND sis_svccode_fileB.csv both attached (ground truth: File A = 0154,0178,0158,0153,0154; File B = 0178,0164,0154,01778,0160).
reproduction: 2. Send: 'Compare the service codes in both files.'
expected: The deterministic `render_multi_csv_result()` path, with each file's own 5 values, never merged, each kept with its own citation.
actual_before_fix: Fell to the ungrounded LLM path, which stated File A's values wrong (dropped 0178, listed 0154 three times instead of two) while File B happened to be correct -- documented in the prior pass's SIS_ServiceCode_FileDB_Failure_Cases.jsonl (CSVCOL-001b).
actual_after_fix: Deterministic table output (📋 UI card, not prose): File B -> row 1: 0178, row 2: 0164, row 3: 0154, row 4: 01778, row 5: 0160 [sis_svccode_fileB.csv, rows 1-5]. File A -> row 1: 0154, row 2: 0178, row 3: 0158, row 4: 0153, row 5: 0154 [sis_svccode_fileA.csv, rows 1-5]. Both exactly match ground truth.
root_cause: Same as CSVCOL-FLINE-001 -- `csv_ops.parse_csv_question()` returned None for the plural phrasing against BOTH files, so `attachment_qa.py`'s `len(csv_docs) >= 2` deterministic branch produced no answer and the question fell through to the LLM.
verified_outcome: Live UI, 2026-10-13 ~16:18, confirmed as a side effect of the CSVCOL-FLINE-001 fix -- no separate code change was needed for this symptom, exactly as predicted in the prior pass's report.

summary: 'What is the difference between F-Line and F-Line Appeal?' named only one code's definition (whichever one the alias/scoring resolved to), never explaining the two services side by side as a real comparison.
reproduction: Before any fix: 'What is the difference between F-Line and F-Line Appeal?' -> the single F-Line (0178) definition, 0185 never mentioned at all (same failure as FLINEAPPEAL-001, since both codes collapsed to one before `find_service_codes()` ever ran).
expected: Both 0178 and 0185 explained, ideally with an explicit same/different verdict.
verified_outcome: Live UI, fresh conversation, no attachment, 2026-10-13 ~16:22: 'What is the difference between F-Line and F-Line Appeal?' -> 'No, F-Line (0178) and F-Line Appeal (0185) are different services under TAMILNILAM Urban. 0178 (F-Line) is the initial boundary demarcation survey request, whereas 0185 (F-Line Appeal) is an appeal against a prior demarcation decision.' followed by both codes' full descriptions. Also verified: 'Are F-Line and F-Line Appeal the same?' gives the same dual-code answer. Fix: `find_service_codes()` in backend/utils/helpers.py now detects BOTH codes when the message carries comparison/pairing language (difference, compare, versus, both, same, ...) via a new `_all_alias_codes()` helper that checks every department alias independently (needed because a separately-made, complementary fix to `_svc_name_alias_match()` elsewhere in the same file now correctly prefers the longer, more specific alias 'f-line appeal' over the shorter 'f-line' -- good for a single-term lookup, but it meant the shorter alias's own code was no longer separately visible to a two-term comparison; `_all_alias_codes()` checks each alias on its own instead of only the single best one). The lead sentence naming 0178 as 'the initial boundary demarcation survey request' and 0185 as 'an appeal against a prior demarcation decision' is a SEPARATE, concurrent addition (backend/services/chatbot.py ~line 1360) not made in this pass -- its wording is grounded in backend/documents/land_rules.txt and tamilnilam_urban_services_and_districts.txt, both of which independently describe 0185 as an appeal survey. Regression test: SIS_ServiceCode_FileDB_Regression_Tests/test_fline_appeal_multicode_comparison.py (6/6 passing).
